title: The tensor algebra is graded by the tensor powers
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $M$ an $R$-module. Let $\mathrm T_R(M)$ be the tensor algebra of $M$ over $R$, the associative $R$-algebra $\bigoplus_{n\ge0}M^{\otimes_R n}$ whose multiplication is concatenation of pure tensors, $(x_1\otimes\dots\otimes x_n)\cdot(y_1\otimes\dots\otimes y_m)=x_1\otimes\dots\otimes x_n\otimes y_1\otimes\dots\otimes y_m$, with $R$-linear map $\iota:M=M^{\otimes_R1}\to\mathrm T_R(M)$, so that the pure tensor $x_1\otimes\dots\otimes x_n$ is the product $\iota(x_1)\cdots\iota(x_n)$. For $n\ge0$ let $\mathrm T^n_R(M)\subseteq\mathrm T_R(M)$ be the $R$-submodule spanned by the products $\iota(x_1)\cdots\iota(x_n)$ with $x_1,\dots,x_n\in M$ (so $\mathrm T^0_R(M)=R\cdot1$ and $\mathrm T^1_R(M)=\iota(M)$). Then $\mathrm T_R(M)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\mathrm T^n_R(M)$ as $R$-modules: every $t\in\mathrm T_R(M)$ is a finite sum $\sum_nt_n$ with $t_n\in\mathrm T^n_R(M)$, and the $t_n$ are uniquely determined by $t$. Moreover $1\in\mathrm T^0_R(M)$ and $\mathrm T^n_R(M)\cdot\mathrm T^m_R(M)\subseteq\mathrm T^{n+m}_R(M)$ for all $n,m\ge0$.
